content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Junior Frontend / Full-Stack Developer
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
github.com/aiyana-bt-example | aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing graduate with hands-on experience building web applications using React and TypeScript, plus project experience developing Node.js/Express APIs and working with PostgreSQL. Strong focus on accessible interfaces, with experience fixing accessibility issues on a live React site and testing a web app with screen readers. Familiar with automated unit testing using Jest and React Testing Library.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Git/GitHub, Figma
Accessibility: WCAG 2.1, keyboard navigation, screen-reader testing, ARIA labels, colour contrast

PROJECTS
Tidewatch — Final Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app presenting tides, water temperature and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast.
- Developed the React and TypeScript frontend, and a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Received a grade of 82% (First Class) and demonstrated the project at the college showcase.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js, Jest.

Yoga Studio Booking Site — Freelance | 2025
- Built marketing pages and a class timetable with booking requests sent by email.
- Used Next.js static generation and Tailwind CSS; deployed on Vercel, with content edited in Markdown files.

Accessible Gallery Component — Harbourline Media | 2024
- Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages and documented it with Storybook stories.
- Technologies: React, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library.

Study Buddy — Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a study-session matching web app developed by a team of four; other team members built the API and database.
- Technologies: React, JavaScript, Firebase Authentication.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance) | Self-employed | Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS.
- Make small updates to two WordPress sites.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin | May 2024–Aug 2024
- Worked with the web team on the company’s React news site.
- Fixed accessibility issues identified in an audit, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels, across 20+ components.
- Built a reusable image gallery component and wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
- Helped approximately 30 students during one semester of web development labs.

Barista (Part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin | 2021–2025

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology | 2021–2025
First Class Honours
Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and easy to scan. It presents strong evidence of React, TypeScript, accessibility, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, testing, and Next.js experience, with useful measurable details such as 20+ components, approximately 30 students, a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100, and an 82% project grade. The project and internship descriptions are particularly relevant to a patient-facing product role. The main content omission is the student hackathon from the candidate information. The CV also needs to distinguish more explicitly between professional experience and academic/personal project experience, because the role asks for 2+ years of professional experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience formatting, plain-text technologies, and ATS-friendly bullet points. It contains strong searchable terms including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, WCAG 2.1, Storybook, Next.js, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, and screen-reader testing. AI/ATS screening probability is good for a junior frontend or junior full-stack profile, but materially lower for this specific role because the document does not demonstrate the required two years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, or health-data privacy awareness. Do not add those terms unless supported by genuine experience. The current formatting appears parsing-friendly; no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual section labels are present.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with the role's React/TypeScript frontend work, accessibility focus, Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL project experience, automated unit testing, Git/GitHub, Next.js, wellness-related booking software, and Storybook. Tidewatch and the yoga studio booking site are especially relevant to Verdane Care's patient-facing booking and accessibility context. English is shown as native. The candidate material does not meet the stated 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience: the documented professional experience consists of a May-August 2024 internship and freelance work from October 2025 onward, while the backend and database experience is primarily project-based. End-to-end testing is not evidenced; the documented testing is unit testing and screen-reader/accessibility testing. Awareness of OWASP/web security fundamentals and health-data privacy requirements is not evidenced. German or Croatian, AWS or an equivalent cloud platform, Docker, analytics, and A/B testing are also not evidenced. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than rewriting defects. The CV otherwise aligns well with the company's accessibility, practical usability, wellness, and patient-focused themes without making unsupported healthcare claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR — In the PROJECTS section, add the documented hackathon as a short project entry, because it demonstrates rapid delivery and additional frontend experience. For example: "Transit Delay Notifier — Student Hackathon | 2024
- Placed 2nd in a 24-hour hackathon; built the frontend as part of a three-person team." Keep the technology list limited to tools actually used, since none are specified in the candidate information.

MINOR — In the PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY, make the professional-versus-project distinction explicit so the CV does not imply two years of professional full-stack experience. For example, change the opening to: "Computing graduate with professional experience from a React accessibility internship and freelance Next.js development, plus project experience building full-stack applications with React, TypeScript, Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL." Retain the existing accessibility and testing evidence after this sentence.

MINOR — In the PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE section under "Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance)," retain the existing truthful description but make the freelance scope clearer by changing the first bullet to: "Built and deployed a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS." This better connects the experience to Verdane Care's appointment-booking domain without claiming healthcare experience.
